builder_plan.baseline: Your current model on identical held-out tasks and the same resource budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, latency, memory, context limits, and migration cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks vs. Multi-Layer Perceptrons: A Rigorous Statistical Benchmark on Clinical Tabular Data
summary: KAN variants replace the tuned MLP as the classifier on structured clinical tabular data. They cost 1.20x-1.48x more inference latency and up to 12.5x more parameters, with no systematic pooled accuracy advantage. Gains are confined to severely imbalanced cohorts (minority-class AUPRC), so adoption on balanced data, or where latency and model size dominate, yields overhead without benefit.
rationale: The paper shows condition-dependent quality gains against a cheap, strong MLP baseline, so KANs warrant targeted validation on imbalanced tabular tasks rather than blanket adoption.
technique: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks for clinical tabular classification

claims.statement: KAN variants replace the tuned MLP as the classifier on structured clinical tabular data. They cost 1.20x-1.48x more inference latency and up to 12.5x more parameters, with no systematic pooled accuracy advantage. Gains are confined to severely imbalanced cohorts (minority-class AUPRC), so adoption on balanced data, or where latency and model size dominate, yields overhead without benefit.

TabKAN and ReLUKAN achieve higher AUPRC than standard MLPs on severely imbalanced datasets, but pooled across datasets KANs show only comparable discrimination, with 1.20x-1.48x longer per-sample inference latency and up to 12.5x more trainable parameters.
